Course Assignments
Course Grading System:
Your comprehension and production skills will be evaluated regularly. You will also be evaluated on your preparation for class activities and your assignments outside of the class. All grades are calculated using weighted percentages. 

Memrise (ungraded)
Memrise will be offered as a tool to help you learn vocabulary but will be ungraded. A minimum of 5 minutes daily reviewing vocabulary is recommended. Students who complete Memrise tend to score much higher on quizzes and tests. So, although this activity is not required, using this app for reviewing vocabulary will often improve performance overall. 

PlayPosit Lectures (10% of grade)
Lectures are pre-recorded with interactive elements like multiple choice questions, polls, fill-in short answers, discussions, and more. Because of the visual nature of ASL students will be asked to submit short videos in GoReact to practice principles outlined in the lectures.  

Workbook assignments & GoReact Discussion Participation (30% of grade)
This workbook is designed to retain and reinforce what is learned in the online lectures and the GoReact discussions give students opportunities to practice with peers.. Complete the assigned workbook assignments and GoReact discussions by the assigned due dates in Canvas. 

Sign On Connect (Q=15% of grade)
Students will meet remotely with a native signer multiple times during the course to practice signing.  The instructor will provide suggestions for topics to cover.  The student may choose to cover other topics during the session, in addition to those suggested by the instructor.  Students will set appointments on their own to fit a flexible schedule.  Sessions will fill, so be sure to schedule early. These meetings are a key component of learning the language and are required.  Missing sessions cannot be substituted with other activities. The lowest grade in this category is dropped. If you miss a session, have technical difficulties, or an ambassador no-shows, it will not affect your grade. If an ambassador no-shows, contact SignOn Connect promptly to request a refund for the minutes. Reschedule at the earliest opportunity, and if the rescheduled date is after the due date, promptly contact your LEAD instructor so they are aware. Be sure to join the class in SignOn using the join code in module 0 so that the lead instructor can see your attendance. The lead instructor will manually update grades periodically throughout the course- typically after each assessment. You do not need to provide any documentation outside of joining the course in SignOn.  Cancelling within 48 hours or no showing for a session will result in forfeiture of your minutes. You can use your lowest dropped grade or you can purchase additional minutes directly from SignOn if you wish to reschedule. 

Quizzes & Tests (Q=35% of grade)
Quizzes will be scheduled in Canvas. You may not make up any quizzes you miss – if you miss the quiz, you will get a zero. The quizzes will be based mainly on the ability to comprehend ASL and cultural information. Questions may also be drawn from the reading/viewing of the TRUE+WAY ASL e-workbook/video, video assignments, vocabulary, and class discussions.

Unit tests will cover all material presented to that point of the class. They will include information from quizzes, TRUE+WAY ASL, class notes, handouts, lectures, vocabulary videos, as well as your comprehension and production skills. There will be no make-up of the tests except under circumstances I deem to be extreme or unique.

Final Receptive Exam (10% of grade)
The Final exam is cumulative and will cover topics from the entire course. The Exam will take place during the last week of class- finals week. An online review will be provided. The receptive exam will be in Canvas. The final will include comprehension information from the workbook, videos shown in and out of class, vocabulary videos, class assignments, and discussions. There will be no make-up of the final exam except under circumstances I deem to be extreme or unique. 
Extra Credit (Up to 5%)
Conversation Starters Quizzes
You can earn up to 5% extra credit in this course by completing optional Conversation Starter quizzes. These quizzes focus on comprehension of more challenging ASL dialogues and are designed to stretch your skills beyond the core material. While not required, they are strongly encouraged as a way to deepen your understanding and improve your grade.
One extra credit quiz is available per module, excluding review or test modules. These quizzes are due at the same time as the other module assignments and follow the standard late work policy. If you are interested in earning this extra credit, it’s important to complete each quiz on time as we move through the course—they cannot be made up at the end of the session.
On-Time Submission Bonus (5 Points per Module)
 Students who submit all assignments in a module on time or early will unlock a special Extra Credit Quiz worth 5 points. This quiz becomes available only after all required assignments in the module are submitted and will automatically lock after the module’s due date.
No late submissions will be accepted for this opportunity.

Task:


One of my students took ASL 101 and received the following grades across four units and a final exam. Using the assignment data provided, analyze whether the student's learning improved, declined, or remained stable over time.

**Short answer:**  
The student started the semester strong (Units 1‑3), maintained high comprehension scores, and earned near‑perfect marks on most quizzes and the SignOn‑Connect meetings. In Unit 4 the pattern breaks down – the production test and the SignOn‑Connect meeting were never submitted, the comprehension test was turned in late and scored much lower, and two workbook/GoReact items are still missing.  The final exam, however, was still respectable (92 %).  **Overall the evidence points to a decline in performance toward the end of the term, even though the student’s earlier work showed clear improvement.**  

Below is a step‑by‑step breakdown of the data that leads to this conclusion.

---

## 1.  How the course is organized

| Category | Weight in final grade | What it measures |
|----------|----------------------|------------------|
| PlayPosit Lectures (incl. GoReact videos) | 10 % | Video‑lecture comprehension & short signed responses |
| Workbook & GoReact Discussions | 30 % | Vocabulary, sentence‑type drills, interactive dialogues |
| SignOn Connect (remote native‑signer meetings) | 15 % (lowest score dropped) | Live signed conversation practice |
| Quizzes & Tests (including unit comprehension/production tests) | 35 % | Receptive (quizzes, unit comp.) and productive (unit prod., final) skills |
| Final Receptive Exam | 10 % | Cumulative receptive knowledge |
| University Survey, Memrise, “Hidden” items | 0 % (extra credit / admin) | Not part of the grade |

Each **unit** (1‑4) contains a *Comprehension Test*, a *Production Test*, a *SignOn‑Connect meeting*, and several quizzes/worksheets.  The final exam covers everything.

---

---

## 3.  Trend analysis

| Metric | Unit 1 | Unit 2 | Unit 3 | Unit 4 | Direction |
|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|-----------|
| **Comprehension test %** | 95 % | 93 % | 94 % | 81 % | ↓ (sharp drop in U4) |
| **Production test %** | 99 % | 99 % | 94 % | 0 % | ↓↓ (complete non‑submission) |
| **SignOn‑Connect %** | 100 % | 100 % | 100 % | 0 % | ↓↓ (missed meeting) |
| **Average quiz %** | 95 % (100,100,86) | 96 % (91,100) – ignoring missing | 98 % (97,100) | 93 % (100,85) – ignoring missing | Roughly stable, slight dip in U4 |
| **Overall unit performance** (comp + prod + SignOn) | **~98 %** | **~97 %** (with lateness) | **~96 %** | **~27 %** (due to zeros) | **Decline** – especially in U4 |

### What the numbers tell us

* **Units 1‑3** – The student consistently scores **≥90 %** on every major assessment, submits everything on time (or only a day late), and earns perfect marks on the live SignOn‑Connect sessions.  This indicates solid, improving mastery of the material.
* **Unit 4** – Two critical components (production test and SignOn‑Connect meeting) were never turned in, and the comprehension test was late and scored only 81 %.  Several workbook/GoReact items are still missing.  The drop from ~95 % to ~27 % in the “big three” assessments signals a **significant decline** in engagement and/or ability.
* **Final exam** – Despite the poor showing in Unit 4, the student still managed a **92 %** on the cumulative receptive exam, suggesting that the underlying receptive knowledge remained relatively strong.

---

## 4.  Category‑level view (as reported in Canvas)

| Category | Percent earned | Interpretation |
|----------|----------------|----------------|
| Lectures & Conversation Starters | **97.94 %** | Very strong – the student watched/listened attentively and completed the short signed responses. |
| Workbook & GoReact Discussions | **95.43 %** | Excellent – most workbook drills and peer dialogues were done correctly. |
| SignOn Connect | **100 %** (average of submitted meetings) | Perfect when the meetings were attended; the zero in Unit 4 drags the overall average down only because the meeting was missed. |
| Quizzes & Tests | **84.95 %** | Lower than the other categories, largely because of the low‑scoring Unit 4 quiz (34/40) and the missed production test. |
| Final Exam | **92 %** | Strong receptive performance despite the Unit 4 slump. |
| **Overall course grade** | **93 %** (≈ A) | Still an “A” overall, but heavily propped up by the early units. |

---

## 5.  Bottom line – Did learning improve, decline, or stay stable?

| Timeframe | Evidence | Verdict |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| **Early term (Units 1‑3)** | High, consistent scores; all assignments submitted; live practice sessions completed. | **Improvement / Stable high performance** |
| **Late term (Unit 4)** | Production test and SignOn‑Connect meeting not submitted; comprehension test late and markedly lower; several workbook items missing. | **Decline** |
| **Overall trajectory** | Starts strong, dips sharply in the final unit, but final exam still decent. | **Overall decline toward the end**, though the student retains a solid base of receptive knowledge. |

**Take‑away for the instructor / advisor:**  
The student demonstrated competence through the first three units. The sharp drop in Unit 4 suggests a possible loss of motivation, time‑management issue, or external problem that prevented completion of the production‑focused assessments. Since the final exam was still strong, the student likely still possesses the receptive knowledge but needs support (or a reminder of the late‑work policy) to re‑engage with the productive components of the course. Offering a brief check‑in or remediation plan could help prevent a similar pattern in future terms.
